summary.title: Blue Green Deployment
summary.one_liner: Blue-green deployment releases software without downtime by running two identical production environments and switching the router between them.
takeaways: Keep two near-identical production environments (blue and green); one is live while the other is used for final testing of the next release.
Cut over by switching the router (or bouncing the web server) to send traffic to the newly tested environment.
Rollback is fast: switch the router back to the previous environment, which stays intact as a backup.
Separate database schema changes from application upgrades, deploying a schema that supports both old and new versions first.
summary.summary: Martin Fowler's short bliki post, written in 2010, describes blue-green deployment as a way to automate cut-over to production with minimal downtime. Two as-identical-as-possible environments exist, one live and one used for final testing; traffic is switched between them via the router. The article covers rollback, handling missed transactions with read-only mode, the same mechanism doubling as hot-standby disaster recovery testing, and a database approach that separates schema changes from application upgrades. A 2015 update adds the database paragraph and further reading references to the Continuous Delivery book.
